Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 28-year-old woman with new-onset left occipital headache since yesterday, moderate to severe intensity, not relieved by ibuprofen.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Headache, started mid-morning yesterday; unusual for the patient.
- Location: Left side, occipital region.
- Character: Intense, throbbing, gradual onset.
- Severity: 8/10.
- No associated symptoms: No nausea, vomiting, visual disturbances, photophobia, fever, neck stiffness, rash, tingling, numbness, or weakness.
- Sleep: Slept through the night.
- No aggravating or relieving factors related to posture or time of day.
- Pain not improved with Nurofen (ibuprofen); dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No previous similar headaches.
- Past medical history: None reported.
- Allergies: None reported.
- Current medications: None aside from single dose of ibuprofen.
- Family history: Mother with hypertension and migraines.
- Social history: Lives with partner; works as designer; denies tobacco, alcohol, or other drug use.
- No recent increase in stress, or change in diet/lifestyle.
- No recent blood pressure checks.
- Preventive care: Not mentioned.

Examination:
- No vital signs documented.
- No examination findings documented.

Impression:
- New-onset, unilateral (left occipital), moderate-severe headache without red flag symptoms; etiology unclear, possible primary headache disorder.

Plan:
- Advise regular use of a different, stronger pain reliever (name not specified) with food, instead of ibuprofen; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Paracetamol can be used concurrently.
- Advise rest and good hydration.
- Safety-netting: Return if pain worsens, new symptoms develop (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness), or recurrent episodes occur.
- Follow up if not improving within 1–2 days or after trial of recommended medications.

Quality checks:

●	Missing elements: Allergies, medication reconciliation, past medical history all asked and answered. Vitals and physical examination not performed or documented. No neurological examination or fundoscopy. Name of “stronger pain relief” not specified.
●	Internal conflicts: None identified.
●	Transcript quality: Clear, all clinically relevant details captured.
